findings.issue_text: [Medium/data] services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95 — Client/role/group removal only cleans up V1 permission state (setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)); there is no equivalent cleanup for the new V2 data. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client (or role/group) that has V2 permissions leaves orphaned resources, scopes and permission policies in the realm's admin-permissions resource server, which getClientsWithPermission will keep iterating forever.

[Low/bug] services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — The removal listener is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ); previously cleanup ran unconditionally. Realms that used fine-grained permissions and then had the feature disabled will no longer clean up permission state when roles/clients/groups are deleted, accumulating stale authorization data.

[Low/bug] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:120-190 — Roughly a dozen overridden methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException. Any reachable caller (e.g., token-exchange permission evaluation via canExchangeTo when both features are enabled, or permission-introspection paths calling resource()/getPermissions()) gets an unhandled runtime exception / 500 instead of a denial or empty result.

[Low/doc_defect] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java — The requireView / requireViewClientScopes javadocs say "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} / {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but these methods are void and throw ForbiddenException (copy-paste from the can* methods; compare the correct requireList() doc).

[Low/bug] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:265-275 — Dead code: private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is never invoked (leftover from the V1 canExchangeTo implementation); the static import of TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the logger field are also unused, suggesting the token-exchange support was stripped incompletely.

[Low/test_gap] tests/.../fgap/PermissionClientTest.java — No test exercises the newly added MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles, and no test covers the combination of an "all clients" permission with per-client permissions (the hasPermission fallback path that switches between the per-client resource and the type resource is only tested in the two mutually exclusive scenarios).

[Low/performance] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:113-135 (getClientsWithPermission/hasGrantedPermission) — A full policy evaluation is executed for every resource of type "Clients" on each client-listing request (and root.realmResourceServer() is re-fetched per resource inside hasGrantedPermission), which scales poorly for realms with many clients and per-client permissions.

[Low/bug] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:215-235 (hasPermission(ClientModel, String)) — When a per-client resource exists, only that resource is evaluated and the "all-clients" grant is relied upon to match via resource type; if per-client resources are ever created without the resource type set (the resource-creation body in getOrCreateResource is not shown/verified here), type-level grants would be silently shadowed for those clients. At minimum this invariant is untested (see issue 6).

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95 — Client/role/group removal only cleans up V1 permission state (setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)); there is no equivalent cleanup for the new V2 data. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client (or role/group) that has V2 permissions leaves orphaned resources, scopes and permission policies in the realm's admin-permissions resource server, which getClientsWithPermission will keep iterating forever.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the listener still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) on ClientRemovedEvent (and similar for roles/groups). This diff introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, where setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. If management(...) resolves to the V2 permission implementation under this feature (as implied by adding MgmtPermissionsV2 + ClientPermissionsV2), client-removal cleanup will now crash rather than disable/cleanup permissions, leaving any authz artifacts untouched. (The finding’s “iterating forever” wording is overstated, but the missing/broken cleanup is diff-grounded.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — The removal listener is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ); previously cleanup ran unconditionally. Realms that used fine-grained permissions and then had the feature disabled will no longer clean up permission state when roles/clients/groups are deleted, accumulating stale authorization data.

adjudication.rationale: In services/.../permissions/AdminPermissions.java the onEvent handler is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent always triggered `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`. This diff-grounded change means that if fine-grained authz data already exists (created while the feature was enabled) but the feature is later disabled, deletions of roles/clients/groups will no longer perform that cleanup/disable step, leaving permission state and related authz artifacts potentially stale/orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:120-190 — Roughly a dozen overridden methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException. Any reachable caller (e.g., token-exchange permission evaluation via canExchangeTo when both features are enabled, or permission-introspection paths calling resource()/getPermissions()) gets an unhandled runtime exception / 500 instead of a denial or empty result.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` and wires it in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`, but many overridden methods in `ClientPermissionsV2` unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.). From the diff alone we can verify the presence of these runtime exceptions and that this implementation will now be returned for V2 client permissions, but we cannot verify any concrete call sites/reachability that would actually trigger them and cause a 500. This is nevertheless a specific, diff-grounded completeness/risk issue created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/.../fgap/PermissionClientTest.java — No test exercises the newly added MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles, and no test covers the combination of an "all clients" permission with per-client permissions (the hasPermission fallback path that switches between the per-client resource and the type resource is only tested in the two mutually exclusive scenarios).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new client scope constant and permission check path (AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles() -> hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)), but PermissionClientTest only exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (see testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creating per-client scopes Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)) and never grants/tests MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE. Also, ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) contains a nontrivial fallback: if no per-client Resource exists it falls back to the type resource ("all-clients") and only proceeds if there are policies on that resource. The added tests cover per-client permissions (testManageOnlyOneClient/testConfigureOnlyOneClient) and "all clients" permissions (testManageAllClients/testViewAllClients) separately, but none explicitly covers behavior when both exist and ensuring the evaluator prefers/combines correctly across the per-client vs type-resource paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:113-135 (getClientsWithPermission/hasGrantedPermission) — A full policy evaluation is executed for every resource of type "Clients" on each client-listing request (and root.realmResourceServer() is re-fetched per resource inside hasGrantedPermission), which scales poorly for realms with many clients and per-client permissions.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(), the code iterates over every authorization resource of type "Clients" via resourceStore.findByType(..., resource -> ...) and, for each resource, calls hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which performs a full root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...)) evaluation. This is O(N) policy evaluations per call and can scale poorly with many client resources/permissions. Additionally, hasGrantedPermission() re-fetches root.realmResourceServer() per resource, adding repeated work inside the loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] services/.../permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:215-235 (hasPermission(ClientModel, String)) — When a per-client resource exists, only that resource is evaluated and the "all-clients" grant is relied upon to match via resource type; if per-client resources are ever created without the resource type set (the resource-creation body in getOrCreateResource is not shown/verified here), type-level grants would be silently shadowed for those clients. At minimum this invariant is untested (see issue 6).

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), the code evaluates ONLY the per-client Resource when it exists (resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)) and falls back to the "all-clients" resource-type resource only when the per-client resource is null. This means a realm-wide grant attached to the Clients resource type can be effectively ignored for any client that happens to already have an individual resource entry (even if that individual resource has no policies/scopes granting access), i.e., type-level permissions can be shadowed by the existence of a per-client resource. The finding’s mention of a missing resource type on the per-client resource isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the shadowing behavior itself is directly implied by the shown logic.
